table.name: Addresses
table.purpose: Postal addresses (street, unit, city, ZIP, state, country) referenced by student, degree program, enrolment and transcript records. One row per address.

col_001.name: address_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate identifier for the address, referenced by Students, Degree_Programs, Transcript_Contents and Student_Enrolment.

col_002.name: street_address
col_002.description: Street line of the address: house number plus street name, sometimes with unit suffix.

col_006.name: postal_code
col_006.description: US ZIP code stored as zero-padded 3-digit text (e.g. '068', '943'); values 068-943.

table.name: Courses
table.purpose: Catalog of courses offered; each row is one course, referenced by sections, enrolments and transcripts.

col_001.name: course_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate identifier for the course, referenced by sections, enrolments, transcripts and student/program tables.

table.name: Degree_Programs
table.purpose: One row per degree program offered by the university; each program belongs to a department and has a degree level (Bachelor/Master/PHD). Referenced by students, enrolments and transcripts.

col_001.name: degree_program_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the degree program; surrogate integer identifier referenced by Students, Transcript_Contents and Student_Enrolment.

col_002.name: department_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to Departments.col_001, identifying the department offering the program. The joins to Addresses and Courses are likely spurious coincidental matches on small integer keys; the Departments join is the semantically meaningful one.

col_003.name: degree_level
col_003.description: Level of the degree: Bachelor, Master, or PHD.

col_004.name: program_name
col_004.description: Name/title of the degree program. Values are mostly distinct Latin-like placeholder words (e.g. 'cumque', 'assumenda'), so it is a free-text name field, though the actual values appear to be synthetic/fake data.

table.name: Departments
table.purpose: A university departments lookup table; each row is one academic department, referenced by degree programs. 15 rows of synthetic/seeded data (col_003 contains lorem-ipsum filler).

col_001.name: department_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each department (1-15). Referenced by Degree_Programs.col_002, which assigns each degree program to a department.

col_002.name: department_name
col_002.description: Unique name of the department (e.g. 'art', 'biology', 'computer science', 'history', 'math').

col_003.name: description
col_003.description: Free-text field, likely a department description or note, but values are lorem-ipsum placeholder words ('consequatur', 'nihil', 'dolorem'), so the intended meaning is uncertain; it is a text annotation of some kind.

table.name: Sections
table.purpose: Course sections offered by the institution: each row is one section of a course, identified by a section code/letter, with a link to the course it belongs to and a descriptive name. Likely referenced by enrolment/transcript tables.

col_001.name: section_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique surrogate identifier for each section (1-15).

col_002.name: course_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to Courses.col_001; the course this section belongs to. Some courses have multiple sections.

col_003.name: section_code
col_003.description: Single-letter section identifier (a, b, c, ...), unique per row; distinguishes parallel sections of the same course.

col_004.name: section_name
col_004.description: Free-text descriptive name/label for the section (Latin-like filler words such as 'voluptatem', 'provident').

table.name: Semesters
table.purpose: Lookup table of academic semesters/terms (e.g. fall, winter, spring, summer of a given year), keyed by a numeric semester id and referenced by scheduling/enrolment tables such as Sections and Student_Enrolment_Courses.

col_001.name: semester_id
col_001.description: Primary key; surrogate integer identifier for each semester (1-15).

col_002.name: term_name
col_002.description: Human-readable term label combining season and year, e.g. 'fall 2010', 'spring 2018', 'summer 2010'. One value ('spring 2018') appears twice, suggesting either a duplicate or two distinct semester records sharing a label.

table.name: Student_Enrolment
table.purpose: One row per course enrolment record, linking a student to a course (and related entities). The table is sparsely populated (15 rows) and several foreign keys are ambiguous because surrogate integer keys overlap across lookup tables.

col_001.name: enrolment_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the enrolment table; a surrogate integer identifier, unique across all 15 rows (values 1-15).

col_002.name: course_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to Courses.col_001, identifying the course the student is enrolled in (many-to-one).

col_003.name: student_id
col_003.description: Likely a foreign key to Students, identifying the enrolled student. No join was accepted by the profiler, but the values (small integers, many-to-one pattern, e.g. value 2 appears 4 times) fit a student reference in an enrolment table. Alternative reading: it could reference another entity such as a section or semester, so this remains tentative.

table.name: Student_Enrolment_Courses
table.purpose: Junction/association table linking a student enrolment to courses; each row represents one course associated with an enrolment, and is referenced by transcript contents. The exact semantics of the two course references are not fully clear from the data.

col_001.name: enrolment_course_id
col_001.description: Primary key of this table; surrogate identifier for the enrolment-course association. Referenced by Transcript_Contents.col_001, so each row corresponds to a line item that can appear on a transcript.

col_002.name: course_id
col_002.description: Reference to Courses.col_001 (course identifier; lookup labels include math, en, cal, ml, pl). Most likely the course the student is enrolled in via this association.

table.name: Students
table.purpose: One row per student: identity and contact details plus links to an address and a degree program.

col_001.name: student_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the Students table; unique integer identifier for each student.

col_002.name: address_id
col_002.description: Reference to Addresses.col_001 (many-to-one), the student's address. The statistics also accept joins to Courses and Degree_Programs, but an address link is the most plausible reading for a student record; the true target is not fully certain.

col_003.name: degree_program_id
col_003.description: Reference to Degree_Programs.col_001 (many-to-one), the student's degree program (Bachelor/Master/PHD). Joins to Addresses and Courses are also statistically accepted, so the target is not fully certain.

col_004.name: first_name
col_004.description: Student's first (given) name; unique across the 15 rows.

col_005.name: middle_name
col_005.description: Student's middle name; unique values, sits between first and last name in column order.

col_006.name: last_name
col_006.description: Student's last (family) name; unique across the 15 rows.

col_007.name: phone_number
col_007.description: Student's phone number in various formats (with/without parentheses, dots, dashes, extensions).

col_010.name: date_of_birth
col_010.description: Timestamps from 1971 to 2018; given the paired later date in col_011, this is most plausibly the student's birth date, though the range extending to 2018 makes this uncertain.

col_011.name: enrollment_date
col_011.description: Timestamps from 1971 to 2017; plausibly the date the student enrolled (or another lifecycle date such as admission). The exact semantic is not certain.

table.name: Transcript_Contents
table.purpose: Line items of a student transcript: each row links a transcript to a specific course enrolment record (from Student_Enrolment_Courses) and identifies the course taken. It is the detail/child table of the Transcripts table, specifying which courses appear on each transcript.

col_001.name: student_enrolment_course_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the specific course enrolment (a row in Student_Enrolment_Courses) that this transcript line item refers to. Many transcript lines can point to the same enrolment record (many_to_one). Values are small surrogate keys (0, 2, 7, 76, 96, ... up to ~70 million), consistent with an auto-generated enrolment-course ID.

col_002.name: course_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the course recorded on this transcript line. The statistics accepted joins to Addresses, Courses, and Degree_Programs because those tables share the same small-ID key space, but the semantic context (a transcript content row) makes Courses the intended target: values 2-15 map to course labels such as math, en, cal, ml, pl. The joins to Addresses and Degree_Programs are spurious coincidences of overlapping ID ranges.

table.name: Transcripts
table.purpose: One row per student transcript (academic record document), likely linked to its line items via the Transcript_Contents table. The table itself carries only an identifier and a date; the actual course/grade details presumably live in Transcript_Contents, which references these rows.

col_001.name: transcript_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the Transcripts table; a surrogate identifier, one unique value per transcript (15 rows, values 1-15, no joins detected here, but presumably referenced by Transcript_Contents).

col_002.name: issue_date
col_002.description: A timestamp associated with each transcript, unique per row, ranging 1975-2013. Most plausibly the date the transcript was issued/generated. Alternative reading: the date the transcript record was created or last updated; the data alone cannot distinguish these, though the wide historical range suggests an issuance or record-creation date rather than a recent modification timestamp.
